items.title: ‘Sole earning member’: The families left behind as FIRs pile up against Sijimali mine protesters
items.summary: A doctor’s arrest on October 16 drew fresh attention to the police action against opponents of Vedanta’s proposed bauxite mine in Odisha’s Sijimali hills. Dr Randall Sequeira is not the only one behind bars. Newslaundry looked at a few other arrests: Laxman Naik, a martial arts instructor arrested alongside Dr Sequeira; Hiramal, a farmer jailed since August; and Lingaraj Azad, an activist held since March. All three are named in multiple FIRs alongside hundreds of unidentified persons, and all have had bail pleas rejected. The FIRs offer a window into the pressure on a movement that began in 2023 across at least 40 villages. Since then, at least 40 cases have been registered. Newslaundry has seen copies of five, which name at least 155 accused and refer to a further 900 unidentified persons. The allegations in them are yet to be tested in court. The mining project will require extensive forest land to be cleared in the Tijimali hill range of the Eastern Ghats and the direct displacement of at least two villages. Many residents depend on farming or herding for their livelihoods. They cultivate rice and vegetables on small plots. The project would force them to move elsewhere. Concer

items.title: TN cops allege suicide after lorry driver found dead in station restroom
items.summary: A 42-year-old lorry driver, who had gone to Chekkanoorani police station in Madurai in connection with a complaint, was found dead in the station's restroom on Saturday, November 14. The police have claimed that he died by suicide. According to reports, the deceased have been identified as Balakrishnan, a resident of Alagarnayakanpatti in Theni district, who worked as a lorry driver for a company involved in transporting goods. On November 3, Balakrishnan was transporting around 60 bags of cardamom from Thevaram in Theni to Madurai when the lorry he was driving allegedly caught fire near Valandur canal in Madurai's Usilampatti area and the fire destroyed the cardamom bags. Following the incident, the company manager, who had sent the cardamom, raised suspicion over missing bags and submitted a complaint to the police. Based on the complaint, the police asked Balakrishnan to appear for an inquiry at Chekkanoorani police station and also to assist the police in examining CCTV footage related to the incident. items.title: Delhi’s toxic air: Athletes must keep training, but many can’t afford to leave
items.summary: With winter in full swing and pollution levels rising, most Delhiites stay indoors. Athletes, however, don't have that option. Even with the GRAP (Graded Response Action Plan) Stage-III in effect and the CAQM (Commission for Air Quality Management) advising postponements of sports competitions, training continues. In this report, Khushi Jaiswal speaks to athletes and coaches in the capital. High-repetition training, they say, demands heavy oxygen intake, and in the polluted air, they bring breathing difficulties, dry throats and persistent coughing. One parent even says that her daughter has been on anti-allergy medication for a week. Some athletes leave Delhi to train in places like Bengaluru, Odisha or hill stations in nearby states, and a few have even gone abroad. But leaving Delhi comes with a cost which many families can't afford. As a result, many are forced to train even when the AQI (air quality index) exceeds 400. Athletes in Delhi University, meanwhile, say that the DU Sports Council tournaments are still going ahead, with no postponements. Watch our report. items.title: Karnataka HC dismisses MLA Yatnal's plea to quash defamation case filed by Congress MLA Patil
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Thursday refused to quash a criminal defamation case filed against expelled BJP MLA Basanagouda Ramangouda Patil Yatnal over remarks he made against Congress MLA Shivananda S Patil during a media interview broadcast on the YouTube channel of Gadinada Kranti on April 30, 2025. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde dismissed a plea filed by Yatnal challenging the criminal proceedings. In doing so, the Court rejected Yatnal's argument that the trial court had erred in taking cognisance of Patil's complaint without first examining a witness who could speak to whether Patil’s reputation had been lowered in that witness's estimation. The High Court held that, at the stage of taking cognisance, a magistrate need not invariably insist on examining a witness other than the complainant to establish that the complainant's reputation has been lowered in the witness's estimation. items.title: Leaving all disputes to arbitration could stall growth of law: Former Supreme Court Justice Ravindra Bhat
items.summary: Leaving all disputes to arbitration could eventually slow the development of law, Former Supreme Court Justice S Ravindra Bhat cautioned even as he acknowledged that Indian courts have increasingly limited their interference with arbitral awards. Speaking at the Dubai Arbitration Week 2026, Justice Bhat said legal principles have evolved through robust judicial enquiry and the limited scope for reviewing arbitral awards raises a broader question about how new legal concepts would develop. “So if you leave everything to arbitration, as we all believe that all disputes should be arbitrable, I think there will be a time when the growth of law will be static,” he said. Justice Bhat was speaking at “Four Courts, One Award: Judicial Perspectives, Cross-Border Advocacy & the Great Common Law Debate” , organised by the Indian Institute of Arbitration and Mediation in association with Balfaqeeh Advocates & Legal Consultants and Providence Law Asia. items.title: ‘Closing meat shops during PM’s visit is fascism’: Former Karnataka HC judge Nagamohan Das
items.summary: Former Karnataka High Court judge HN Nagamohan Das on Friday, November 13, criticised the closure of meat shops in parts of Bengaluru’s Anekal taluk ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit. He called the directive an instance of fascism and an infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights. “The right to food is a fundamental right. You eat what you want, let them eat what they want, and let me eat what I want. Who are you to come and dictate what we eat?” Nagamohan Das said. His remarks came after the Bengaluru Urban district administration ordered the closure of meat shops within the limits of Jigani Town Municipal Council and Kallubalu Gram Panchayat in Anekal taluk from 6 am on November 12 to 4 pm on November 13. The order was issued ahead of Modi’s visit to the area for the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram. items.title: BJP leader and ex-Mizoram Governor Sreedharan Pillai designated Senior Advocate by Kerala High Court suo motu
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has suo motu conferred Senior Advocate designation to Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader PS Sreedharan Pillai . Pillai is a doyen at the bar and an expert in criminal law matters. Pillai has previously served as the State President of the BJP and as the Governor in Mizoram and Goa. In a full court meeting held on November 11, the High Court conferred him Senior Advocate designation. Seventeen other lawyers were also conferred Senior Advocate designation at this meeting. However, those lawyers had submitted applications to be considered for conferment of the title. Pillai was conferred the gown by the Court on its own under Rule 3(2) of the High Court of Kerala (Designation of Senior Advocates) Rules, 2026. The rule empowers the full court to confer the designation by consensus to any advocate who is in its opinion, "a person of exceptional quality, eminence and has special expertise in any field of law." items.title: Can Brahmins get OBC quota by converting to Christianity? Madras High Court expresses surprise
items.summary: The Madras High Court has expressed surprise over a claim that even Brahmins can get Other Backward Classes (OBC) reservation benefits by converting to Christianity and joining the Church of South India (CSI) under Tamil Nadu's existing reservation framework. [Kodeeswaran Vs State] A Division Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi observed that such a possibility, if established, warrants serious reconsideration of the existing system. "The petitioner's counsel startled us by asserting that if a Brahmin gets converted and joins CSI denomination, he can enjoy OBC status as per the present statutory framework. If this assertion is true, then a serious re-think is certainly vindicated," the Court said. Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi The submission was made before the Court during the hearing of a plea challenging the constitutional validity of provisions granting Backward Class (BC) and Most Backward Class (MBC) status to several Christian communities and Christian converts in Tamil Nadu. G Kodeeswaran, a Kallar community member and TNPSC examination applicant, challenged the reservation benefits granted to the Christian communities and converts under Tamil Nadu law.
